# GMEOW Norms Module

The GMEOW Norms Module — generalized deontics with indexed authority (issues #351 / #352, EPIC #348).

**IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/norms>  
**CURIE:** `gmeow:slices/norms`  

**Type:** `owl:Ontology`  

Generalized deontics with indexed authority — the constitutional keystone of the normative stack (EPIC #348).

DOCTRINE.
  * THERE IS NO OUGHT, ONLY OUGHT-ACCORDING-TO. Every norm names its issuer (gmeow:normIssuer); an ought without an issuer is the deontic analogue of a global truth axiom and is forbidden by SHACL. Two contradictory normative systems coexist without inconsistency because neither is asserted — both are recorded as issued (Principles 1, 9; the deception module's held/projected move applied to oughts). normIssuer ⊑ gmeow:accordingTo is documented, not axiomatised, because accordingTo is an AnnotationProperty and normIssuer is an ObjectProperty — the vantage ⊑ accordingTo precedent (standpoint module).
  * PRECEDENCE IS DATA, NOT SEMANTICS. gmeow:overrides is pairwise and deliberately NOT transitive: lex-superior chains are solver inferences, never reasoner entailments. AuthorityLevel is an ordered value vocabulary (the kernel GranularityLevel pattern — third use); ordering comparisons are solver work (Principle 12). 'Tier 2 overrode X until v3.5' is a gmeow:PrecedenceTenure — the StandpointTenure idiom (Principle 10: withdrawal by suppression, never deletion).
  * CONDITIONS ARE STORED, NEVER EXECUTED. A gmeow:Condition is an InformationObject whose canonical form is prose (conditionText); formalizations (SPARQL ASK, CEL, Rego, Cedar, XACML, SHACL) attach as ConditionExpressions, and EACH FORMALIZATION IS A CLAIM of equivalence to the prose, challengeable through the statement layer. Whether a condition held is a gmeow:ConditionEvaluation — a vantage-indexed Observation — never a graph entailment. No CI step, test, or tool may evaluate a ConditionExpression against the graph as part of validation (the Principle 12 boundary made operational; see docs.md).
  * THE RIGHTS GRAFT (#352) lands here, extension-side, with ZERO core churn: gmeow:Rule ⊑ gmeow:Norm plus subproperty grafts. The deontic trio (Permission / Prohibition / Duty) is NOT an inferior duplicate of Norm + deonticModality — it is a rigid subkind partition (fixed modality per subkind) under the open modality axis, kept for the asset case and its projection affordances. When this extension is absent, the core rights slice behaves exactly as before.
  * Deontic force ranges over teleology: gmeow:prescribedConduct points at event types, goals (#350), situations, or rights actions; its range is intentionally open (the tenurePosition precedent) so the graft needs no dual-typing and the generated schema surface keeps a clean property.
  * ALIGNMENTS DEFERRED to the compiler-arc window (the wip-aboutness-349 precedent): ODRL 2.2 (EDOAL — odrl:Constraint ↔ Condition is structural), LegalRuleML (<Override> ↔ overrides/PrecedenceTenure — the one target where precedence survives round-trip), LKIF-Core, DPV, SUMO normative attributes, UFO-L. Target list is fixed in #351.
